title: Your first session with PanCode
description: Connect a model, open a repository, and ask PanCode to explain how it builds and runs its tests.
author: Anthony Kougkas

title: Desktop or terminal: find your workspace
description: See both interfaces, learn how to launch them, and choose where to start your next coding session.
author: Anthony Kougkas

title: Let PanCode work without watching every call
description: Check the sandbox, undo a change with /rewind, tell the safety judge about your machine, and know when yolo is the right call.
author: Anthony Kougkas

title: Run a playbook from plan to commit
description: Run the built-in sdlc playbook on one task, watch it work, and read the three commits it makes on your branch.
author: Anthony Kougkas

title: Run it unattended within limits
description: Start a headless run with a cost ceiling and a timeout, ask read-only questions, schedule turns, and know what stops each one.
author: Anthony Kougkas

title: Script PanCode in CI
description: Build a CI job on one JSON result, typed exit codes, run limits, a dry run, and an answer validated against your schema.
author: Anthony Kougkas

title: See what a session cost and what a run did
description: Read session cost and stop reasons from local journals, verify a sealed record, and prepare an archive that uploads nothing.
author: Anthony Kougkas

title: A numerical change, checked with PanCode
description: Follow a temperature-conversion example through a floating-point test failure, a correction, and recorded verification.
author: Anthony Kougkas

title: Choose a model for your project
description: Connect a local server, a cloud API, or a supported subscription route, then choose models separately for conversation and delegated work.
author: Anthony Kougkas

title: Coordinate the coding agents you already use
description: Hand a bounded task to a coding agent you have installed, tell a managed run from an interactive handoff, and review what comes back before you combine it.
author: Anthony Kougkas

title: Keep a long coding task on track
description: See what fills the context, carry your decisions through a handoff, and resume the right branch of a long task.
author: Anthony Kougkas

title: Check a change against your repository
description: Name the checks that matter, run them through verify, and see whether a passing result still matches the files you are reviewing.
author: Anthony Kougkas

title: Add skills and plugins deliberately
description: Preview a project skill or plugin, inspect its package pin, and load only what your task needs; installing is not a permission grant.
author: Anthony Kougkas

title: Work from a laptop with remote workers
description: Coordinate workers on other machines over SSH from your laptop, once each node has the same PanCode version and the project at the same path.
author: Anthony Kougkas

title: Write an extension with declared capabilities
description: Scaffold, test, and install a small extension, and see exactly what approving its capabilities covers.
author: Anthony Kougkas

title: Diffusion models in the terminal
description: Connect Inception's Mercury models for chat and workers, and watch an answer refine as a whole instead of arriving token by token.
author: Anthony Kougkas
basis: Documented workflow, without a live Mercury run

title: Panes and docks: files and workers
description: Show and hide a file browser and a live worker dashboard beside the terminal conversation with one key each.
author: Anthony Kougkas
status: Experimental, off by default, needs Herdr

title: Keep named files with the models you chose
description: Declare which paths and tool results may reach which model targets, approve the policy, and see a request to any other destination refused.
author: Anthony Kougkas

title: Search by meaning and record worker runs
description: Index code, memory, and experiment folders with a local embedding model, and attach a redacted terminal recording to a worker's evidence.
author: Anthony Kougkas

title: Run PanCode on a local model
description: Connect a local server with no account or key, check what PanCode learned about it, and see what else to check if code must stay on your machine.
author: Anthony Kougkas

title: Pre-register a benchmark before you measure
description: Use the experiment-protocol skill to lock thresholds, tolerances, and verdict conditions into a contract you commit before any result exists.
author: Anthony Kougkas

title: Keep results outside the tree with the project store
description: Store a result with a note, check it for drift, read it from a script, and let a worker write into one granted tag.
author: Anthony Kougkas

title: Set up a lab from one setup file
description: Write one YAML file that connects every lab member to your model gateway, check what it may carry, and test the route.
author: Anthony Kougkas

title: Share a folder with a teammate or a second terminal
description: Run two sessions in one project, keep each person's state private, and commit project settings that can only make PanCode stricter.
author: Anthony Kougkas

title: Run a research campaign and a blind arena
description: Keep a speed-up only when a measurement proves it and the answers still match, then compare model answers without knowing which model wrote them.
author: Anthony Kougkas

title: Report a problem without leaking your machine
description: Draft a bug report, read the exact text with your paths, names and keys masked, choose how it leaves, and share a diagnostic bundle only if you want to.
author: Anthony Kougkas

title: Ask several agents at once
description: Poll two to five agents on one question and read the vote, or give a council roster one task and let a judge write a single answer.
author: Anthony Kougkas
